summary: 29-year-old woman with known left-sided UC: 9 bloody stools/day, HR 104, T 37.9 °C, Hb 10.1, ESR 42, CRP 68 — Truelove and Witts acute severe colitis. Admit, IV corticosteroids, stool culture and C. difficile, flexible sigmoidoscopy with biopsies (CMV), VTE prophylaxis, avoid antimotility drugs/opioids/NSAIDs, day-3 assessment.

inputs.hpi: Known left-sided ulcerative colitis for 4 years on mesalazine. Five days of 9 bloody stools a day, including at night, with urgency and cramping lower abdominal pain. Feels feverish. No recent antibiotics, no travel, no sick contacts. Not on steroids. No NSAIDs.

exam.abdomen: Mildly distended, tender over the left colon, no guarding or peritonism. Bowel sounds present.

imaging.name: AXR
imaging.result: No colonic dilatation (transverse colon 4.8 cm). Oedematous left colon. No free gas.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute severe ulcerative colitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute severe ulcerative colitis (Truelove and Witts: 9 bloody stools/day, HR 104, T 37.9, Hb 10.1, ESR 42). Admit for IV corticosteroids.

mustNotMiss.note: Infection (C. difficile, enteric pathogens) is excluded in every flare.

emergencyLevel.note: Acute severe UC is a medical emergency needing admission.

recommended.knownGapNote: No Truelove-Witts (or Oxford day-3) calculator or CDS rule on web; CDS suggests Alvarado, TG18 cholangitis and Ranson.
recommended.proposedFix: Add Truelove and Witts (≥ 6 bloody stools + HR > 90, T > 37.8, Hb < 10.5 g/dL, ESR > 30) and the Oxford day-3 rule (> 8 stools, or 3–8 with CRP > 45) to clinical-scales with a CDS trigger on UC.

mustInclude.note: Unprepared flexible sigmoidoscopy with biopsies (including for CMV) within 72 h.
BSG 2019: pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for all inpatients with ASUC, despite rectal bleeding.

mustExclude.note: ASUC without peritonism: an emergency appendicectomy plan is a contraindicated operation. The exam text records "no guarding or peritonism".
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web computeClinicalPrompts fires "Appendicitis — emergency surgical indication" and adds the full "LAPAROSCOPIC APPENDICECTOMY — OPERATIVE PLAN" whenever examAbdomen contains "guarding" or "rebound" — including negated text ("no guarding") and localised guarding from other causes.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Gate the appendicectomy operative-plan prompt on the confirmed working diagnosis (appendicitis) or imaging, not on the words "guarding"/"rebound"; add negation handling (no/without/absent) to exam() matching.

mustExclude.note: Antimotility agents, opioids, anticholinergics and NSAIDs can precipitate toxic megacolon in ASUC.
Truelove and Witts: ≥ 6 bloody stools/day plus HR > 90, T > 37.8 °C, Hb < 10.5 g/dL or ESR > 30 mm/h. WBC is not a criterion; a key point that says "WBC > 10.5" misstates the Hb criterion.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: The ulcerative_colitis protocol key point reads "Truelove-Witts criteria: HR > 90, temp > 37.8 °C, WBC > 10.5, > 6 stools/day" — the criterion is Hb < 10.5 g/dL (and ESR > 30), not WBC.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Correct the key point in lib/pane-engine management protocols (colorectalHerniaBreast.ts, ulcerative_colitis): "≥ 6 bloody stools/day plus HR > 90, T > 37.8 °C, Hb < 10.5 g/dL or ESR > 30 mm/h".

guideline.name: BSG consensus guidelines — management of inflammatory bowel disease in adults
guideline.section: ASUC defined by the Truelove and Witts criteria (Truelove SC, Witts LJ. Br Med J 1955;2:1041–8): ≥ 6 bloody stools daily plus any of fever > 37.8 °C, pulse > 90, Hb < 10.5 g/dL, ESR > 30 mm/h. ASUC: admission, stool culture and C. difficile, flexible sigmoidoscopy with biopsies, IV corticosteroids, VTE prophylaxis, avoid antimotility/opioids/NSAIDs, day-3 assessment
guideline.citation: Lamb CA, Kennedy NA, Raine T, et al. British Society of Gastroenterology consensus guidelines on the management of inflammatory bowel disease in adults. Gut. 2019;68(Suppl 3):s1–s106.

guideline.name: ECCO guidelines on therapeutics in ulcerative colitis — medical treatment
guideline.section: Intravenous corticosteroids first-line for acute severe UC
guideline.citation: Raine T, Bonovas S, Burisch J, et al. ECCO guidelines on therapeutics in ulcerative colitis: medical treatment. J Crohns Colitis. 2022;16:2–17.

guideline.name: Oxford (Travis) criteria — predicting outcome in severe ulcerative colitis
guideline.section: Day 3: > 8 stools/day, or 3–8 stools/day with CRP > 45 mg/L, predicts colectomy
guideline.citation: Travis SP, Farrant JM, Ricketts C, et al. Predicting outcome in severe ulcerative colitis. Gut. 1996;38:905–910.

guideline.name: ECCO guidelines — prevention, diagnosis and management of infections in IBD
guideline.section: Exclude C. difficile in every flare; CMV in steroid-refractory colitis
guideline.citation: Kucharzik T, Ellul P, Greuter T, et al. ECCO guidelines on the prevention, diagnosis, and management of infections in inflammatory bowel disease. J Crohns Colitis. 2021;15:879–913.

rationale: Base IBD case: a typical ASUC admission. Tests the admission level, IV steroids, infection exclusion, VTE prophylaxis (often omitted because of bleeding) and the absence of antimotility drugs. Also checks the protocol’s Truelove-Witts key point.
